content_preview.title: Go 1.27.4 and 1.26.11 Patch 12 CVEs, Eleven of Them Cgo Build-Time Code Execution Bugs
content_preview.summary: The Go team's November 10 security releases close eleven cgo and toolchain flaws that let a malicious dependency run code during a build, plus one net/http crash bug.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The Go team shipped Go 1.27.4 and Go 1.26.11 on November 10, 2026, according to the [official Go release notes](https://go.dev/doc/devel/release), with both point releases carrying security fixes to cgo, the `go` command, the compiler, the linker, and the `net/http` package. The [release announcement mirrored on the oss-sec mailing list](https://seclists.org/oss-sec/2026/q4/646) puts the total at 12 CVEs. According to [SecurityOnline](https://securityonline.info/go-security-fixes-1-...

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece (Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know), 697 words, within the 400-1200 News range. Clear, neutral explanation of eleven related cgo/toolchain build-time code-execution CVEs plus one unrelated net/http crash bug. Appropriately hedges with 'According to' / 'per the announcement' attributions throughout.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 7 source snapshots read in full from sources/2026-11/go-1274-and-12611-patch-12-cves-eleven-of-them-cgo-build-time-code-execution-bugs/ (source-0 through source-6), sha256 of each decompressed file matches the manifest, and no suspicious_patterns were flagged in the manifest. source-0 (go.dev/doc/devel/release) confirms go1.27.4 and go1.26.11 both released 2026-11-10 with security fixes to cgo, the go command, compiler, linker and net/http, verbatim. source-1 (seclists.org oss-sec/646, the Go team's release announcement) verbatim-confirms all 12 CVE descriptions, the 11 cgo CVE numbers (97033-97043), the unrelated net/http CVE (97054), and the researcher credits (Jakub Ciolek for 97054, Ali Sherif for 97036, RyotaK of GMO Flatt Security for 97040 and 97041); every quoted fragment in the article's bullet list matches this source word-for-word. source-2 (seclists.org oss-sec/532, the Nov 5 pre-announcement) verbatim-confirms the 'during US business hours on Tuesday, November 10' and 'PRIVATE security fixes to the standard library and the toolchain' quotes and the full 12-CVE-ID list with no details disclosed. source-3 (securityonline.info) confirms the 11-cgo/1-net-http framing, the 1 critical/10 high/1 medium severity breakdown, the 9.8 highest score on CVE-2026-97040, the 'go build' supply-chain-risk quote, and the recommended mitigations (install 1.27.4/1.26.11, rebuild CI containers, review cgo/.syso dependencies, consider CGO_ENABLED=0) verbatim. source-4 (app.opencve.io) confirms CVSS 3.1 9.8 Critical for CVE-2026-97040 and the affected-version ranges (cmd/go, cmd/link: before 1.26.11, and 1.27.0 up to but excluding 1.27.4) directly from the embedded official CVE JSON record (source security@golang.org / CISA-ADP). source-5 (krakend.io) confirms KrakenD's own advisory restates the CVE-2026-97033 mechanics (--sysroot, -target, -isysroot, -Wl,-syslibroot, -x) verbatim while noting the advisory does not affect KrakenD itself (a build-time-only issue). source-6 (freenode.net) confirms the 12-CVE count and the Nov 5 pre-announcement timing, and is the sole source for the quoted phrase 'details ... private until the releases land, in line with the project's security policy' - see concerns below on freenode.net's confirmability. Allowlist: added seclists.org, securityonline.info and app.opencve.io to config/source_allowlist.txt in this review (confirmed: seclists.org is Insecure.org/Nmap's established mailing-list archive; securityonline.info ('Daily CyberSecurity') has a named founder/editor byline, Do Son; app.opencve.io displays the authoritative CVE record with per-field sourcing). Added krakend.io as KrakenD's own first-party vendor site. freenode.net was NOT added - its /about page (fetched live, since the snapshot itself doesn't carry the masthead) names no editorial staff and the article byline is the pseudonym 'segfault', failing the policy's 'masthead, named staff byline' bar; see corrections record. Anthropic disclosure: not required - the article does not mention Anthropic or an Anthropic-owned/operated product.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Claim-accuracy pass against raw source text found one subordinate error, filed as a correction (see below): the 'What We Don't Know' section's absence claim that cited sources give no individual CVSS scores for the other 11 CVEs beyond SecurityOnline's aggregate breakdown is false - SecurityOnline's own 'Notable CVEs' table lists individual CVSS 3.1 scores (8.8) for seven of those CVEs (97033, 97034, 97035, 97036, 97037, 97038, 97041) plus the 9.8 already cited for 97040. Checked quantifiers/absence terms ('eleven', 'twelfth', 'none of the cited sources report confirmed active exploitation') against every source: 'eleven of the twelve ... cgo' holds (11 numbered CVEs, 97033-97043); 'none ... confirmed active exploitation' holds (source-3 explicitly says 'No exploitation in the wild has been reported' and source-4's SSVC data shows 'Exploitation: none'). Derived figures (CVSS 9.8, severity breakdown, affected-version range) were recomputed/cross-checked against the raw CVE record in source-4, not merely copied from prose. Researcher credits and CVE-number-to-flaw mappings all trace exactly to source-1. Headline, summary and lead hold up against the sources (not in error) - the 'What We Don't Know' error is subordinate.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and attribution-heavy throughout; no sensationalism, no AI self-reference, no promotional language. Appropriately distinguishes the Herald's own framing from quoted/attributed source claims.
editor_notes.originality: Not a duplicate. A prior article (src/content/articles/2026-10/17-go-1272-and-1269-ship-security-fixes-...) covered the separate Go 1.27.2/1.26.9 security release from October; this submission covers a distinct, later release (1.27.4/1.26.11, Nov 10) with an entirely different CVE set. No overlapping facts or angle.
concerns: 'What We Don't Know' overstates an absence: it says the sources give no individual CVSS scores for the other 11 CVEs beyond the aggregate breakdown, but SecurityOnline's own table lists individual 8.8/9.8 scores for 8 of them. Filed as a correction.

The Overview's quote 'details ... private until the releases land, in line with the project's security policy' is attributed solely to freenode.net, an outlet whose /about page names no editorial staff or masthead (pseudonymous byline 'segfault'), which does not meet the policy's reputable-outlet bar. The substance is independently consistent with the Nov 5 pre-announcement's CVE-IDs-only format, but the quoted language itself rests only on the unconfirmed outlet. Filed as a clarification.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Substantively accurate, well-sourced News coverage of a real Go security release with two recoverable, subordinate issues (a wrong absence-claim about CVSS score granularity, and a quote resting on an unconfirmed outlet) that a corrections record can honestly cover without touching the headline, summary or lead. Featured candidacy: 1 - solid, accurate toolchain-security coverage for a defined Go-developer/CI-maintainer audience; not broad-audience or industry-changing.
